key_insight: This paper suggests that vision-language pretraining does not necessarily make text representations globally more aligned with human reading behavior than matched language-only models. In a strictly text-only setting, the multimodal training advantage appears limited or context-dependent rather than universal.
problem_solved: The study addresses whether adding visual-language training makes model representations more human-like during natural reading, without the confounding influence of online visual input or cross-modal fusion.
method: Compare tightly matched LLM and VLM pairs under the same text-only reading conditions.
Isolate the effect of multimodal training history by removing direct visual inputs during evaluation.
Assess human alignment during natural reading to test whether VLMs better predict or reflect human language processing.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this cautions against assuming that multimodal pretraining automatically improves human alignment in text tasks. It highlights the need to evaluate VLMs carefully and task-specifically, especially when using them as cognitive or linguistic models.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison diagram of LLM vs. VLM under text-only evaluation
Pipeline graphic showing training history versus evaluation setting
Bar chart or heatmap of human alignment scores across model pairs
Icon set for text, vision, and brain/human reading alignment
paper_title: VLMs May Not Globally Enhance Human Alignment over LLMs During Natural Reading
paper_authors: Jinzhou Wu, Zhengwu Ma, Jixing Li, Baoping Tang, Zitong Lu
